articles.title: $50M EVO Entertainment Destination Breaks Ground in Downtown Clearwater
articles.summary: A major entertainment destination with a projected $50 million investment has cleared its site in downtown Clearwater, signaling continued strong capital flow into large-format FEC development. EVO Entertainment is known for combining bowling, cinema, arcade, and dining under one roof. This project represents a significant bet on urban entertainment destinations and is worth watching for operators and investors tracking the sector's growth trajectory.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's Lee Cowie outlines how AI and data analytics are pushing ticketing and in-park purchasing well beyond their traditional functions, with a focus on removing friction between guests and experiences. For FEC operators, the shift toward seamless, data-driven guest journeys has direct implications for revenue optimization and customer retention. The piece connects well to broader industry momentum around frictionless operations.

articles.title: InPark Issue 111: Frictionless Guest Experience Takes Center Stage
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's Issue 111 editorial explores how removing operational friction — from ticketing to in-park purchasing to attraction access — is becoming the defining priority for attractions operators. The frictionless experience theme has direct relevance for FEC operators looking to streamline guest flow and boost per-cap spending. This issue serves as a useful strategic read for operators planning technology investments.

articles.title: Six Flags Fiesta Texas Breaks Ground on World's Longest Family Launch Coaster
articles.summary: Six Flags Fiesta Texas has begun construction on Werewolf Gorge, billed as the world's longest family launch coaster and the park's largest single-attraction investment in its history, set to debut in 2027. The project underscores the continued industry emphasis on family-oriented thrill attractions as a key driver of repeat visitation. FEC operators should note the competitive pressure this creates for regional entertainment destinations in Texas.

articles.title: 360Golf System Turns Mini Golf Into Smart, Competitive Social Gaming
articles.summary: Holovis's 360Golf platform uses smart golf balls and HoloTrac sensor technology to automate scoring, introduce bonus challenges, and deliver operator analytics — transforming traditional mini golf into a tech-driven competitive social experience. For FEC operators, the system addresses key pain points around guest engagement, throughput, and operational data collection. The gamification layer and analytics dashboard make it a strong candidate for venues looking to modernize their mini-golf offering.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Its Competitive Socializing Portfolio
articles.summary: Jora Vision is growing its offering in the competitive socializing space, designing experiences where a broad range of guest skill sets can contribute to group play. This is a fast-growing segment that overlaps directly with FEC offerings such as axe throwing, darts, bowling, and arcade-style attractions. Operators evaluating new competitive socializing concepts should take note of Jora Vision's design approach.

articles.title: Premium Interactive Horror: How Six Flags and Warner Bros. Are Raising the Halloween Bar
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences have jointly invested in a premium interactive horror experience called The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, signaling a shift toward higher-ticket, immersive seasonal events. The strategy of layering IP-driven, interactive scares onto existing park infrastructure is increasingly relevant for FECs that run Halloween events. Operators can draw lessons here on how to tier pricing and elevate seasonal programming.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center Bringing Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola
articles.summary: A new Launch Family Entertainment Center featuring an arcade and trampoline park is coming soon to Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, adding to the chain's growing national footprint. The opening reflects continued expansion of multi-attraction FEC concepts into mid-size markets. Operators in the Southeast should monitor this development as Launch grows its competitive presence.

articles.title: What to Know About the Incoming Launch Family Entertainment Center in Pensacola
articles.summary: A follow-up profile on the Launch Family Entertainment Center opening in Pensacola details the center's mix of trampoline attractions, arcade games, and party offerings. The piece provides a useful look at how the Launch brand positions itself in new markets. FEC operators competing in similar markets can use this for competitive benchmarking.

articles.title: Six Flags St. Louis Rebrands as Mid America Adventure
articles.summary: Six Flags St. Louis has officially relaunched under the new name Mid America Adventure, complete with a refreshed logo and brand identity that emphasizes the park's 55-year regional heritage. The rebrand is part of the broader Six Flags and Cedar Fair merger integration, which is reshaping park identities across the country. FEC operators and regional competitors should track how rebranding affects consumer perception and attendance in this market.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large family entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, marking a notable exit in a competitive regional market. The closure is a reminder of the operational and financial pressures facing legacy FEC venues, particularly those that have not reinvested in modernizing their attractions mix. Industry observers and investors should treat this as a case study in the risks of stagnation in the FEC space.

articles.title: Endless Surf and Flowstate Partner to Bring AI-Powered Vision to Surf Parks
articles.summary: Endless Surf and Flowstate have announced a strategic partnership that pairs flexible wave technology with AI-powered computer vision to create a more connected operational and guest experience ecosystem for surf parks. The integration allows for personalized wave experiences and richer operator data — a model increasingly relevant to other tech-enabled FEC attractions. Operators in the active entertainment space should watch how this AI-plus-hardware model develops.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Sees Summer 2026 Growth But Faces Rising Cost Pressures
articles.summary: India's amusement sector posted strong attendance growth in summer 2026, but operators are feeling the squeeze from rising costs that are compressing margins across the industry. The dynamic mirrors challenges faced by FEC operators in other growth markets navigating post-pandemic demand surges alongside inflation. Suppliers and investors with exposure to emerging markets should pay close attention to how Indian operators respond to this margin pressure.

articles.title: India's IAAPI Pushes for GST Reform to Fuel Amusement Industry Growth
articles.summary: The International Amusement and Attractions Park Industry association in India is calling on the government to rationalize GST tax rates to reduce the cost burden on consumers and support sector growth. Tax policy changes in India's large and fast-growing FEC and amusement market could significantly alter the competitive landscape and investment attractiveness of the region. Internationally focused suppliers and investors should monitor this regulatory development.

articles.title: Six Flags Darien Lake Drops Fright Fest in Favor of Family-Friendly Halloween Programming
articles.summary: Six Flags Darien Lake has discontinued its annual Fright Fest horror event for 2026, pivoting instead to family-friendly daytime Halloween programming including Kids Boo Fest and an expanded Oktoberfest. The move reflects a deliberate strategy to capture a broader family demographic during the fall season rather than competing in the increasingly crowded premium horror event space. FEC operators planning their own Halloween programming can use this as a data point on demographic targeting for seasonal events.

articles.title: Kaiqi Group: China's Leading FEC and Play Environment Manufacturer Eyes Global Growth
articles.summary: Kaiqi Group, one of China's largest designers and manufacturers of non-powered play and FEC solutions, operates over 100,000 square metres of manufacturing facilities and has installed products in more than 120 countries. The company positions itself as an end-to-end partner offering master planning, thematic design, IP integration, and operational support for FECs, theme parks, and mixed-use developments. For FEC operators evaluating play equipment suppliers or exploring new venue concepts, Kaiqi represents a significant global manufacturing option.

articles.title: New Family Entertainment Center Opens in Rock Springs, Wyoming
articles.summary: A new family entertainment center has opened in Rock Springs, Wyoming, bringing additional indoor entertainment options to a smaller regional market. The opening continues a pattern of FEC development reaching beyond major metro areas into mid-size and smaller cities. Operators and franchisors eyeing secondary market expansion will find this a useful data point on market appetite.

articles.title: Fresno Bed Bath & Beyond Space Gets New Indoor Entertainment Tenant
articles.summary: A vacant Bed Bath & Beyond retail space in Fresno, California has been leased to an indoor entertainment operator, adding to a growing national trend of FEC concepts backfilling former big-box retail locations. This real estate dynamic continues to create opportunities for FEC expansion in markets with affordable large-footprint spaces. Operators and developers exploring venue acquisition strategies should take note of this ongoing retail conversion trend.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Designing Interactive Themed Experiences
articles.summary: Alterface, a specialist in interactive dark ride and experience design, is marking its 25th anniversary with a look back at the company's philosophy of creating what it calls invisible magic — seamless interactivity that enhances storytelling without calling attention to the technology. The company's experience designing multi-player interactive systems is directly applicable to FEC dark rides, shooting galleries, and interactive attractions. Operators exploring interactive attraction upgrades will find Alterface's portfolio and approach worth examining.

articles.title: Mr. Putters Expands Indoor Mini Golf and Entertainment Offerings Across Tampa Bay
articles.summary: Mr. Putters is expanding its indoor entertainment footprint across Tampa Bay, marketing its mini golf and entertainment offerings to families, schools, and corporate clients. The multi-segment approach — targeting both leisure and group sales channels — is a model increasingly used by FEC operators to maximize venue utilization across the week. Operators looking to diversify revenue streams beyond walk-in traffic should review Mr. Putters' group sales strategy.

articles.title: Family Restaurant Entertainment Concept Proposed for Grand Forks, North Dakota
articles.summary: A new family restaurant and entertainment hybrid experience has been proposed for a Franklin on Fourth location in Grand Forks, combining dining with entertainment in a format that continues to gain traction across the FEC industry. The dining-entertainment hybrid model has been one of the sector's strongest growth formats in recent years, driven by consumers seeking combined food and activity experiences. Local operators and franchisors should watch this proposal as an indicator of format viability in smaller markets.

articles.title: Apex Entertainment Renews Partnership with New England Patriots Kicker Andy Borregales
articles.summary: Apex Entertainment has renewed its community partnership with New England Patriots kicker Andy Borregales and the New England Center For Children, extending a local sports celebrity tie-in for the regional FEC brand. Athlete and sports team partnerships can be a cost-effective brand awareness and community engagement tool for FEC operators competing against larger entertainment venues. This renewal demonstrates the ongoing value Apex sees in local sports marketing as a customer acquisition strategy.

articles.title: Play Town Indoor Amusement Center Proposed for Milford, Connecticut
articles.summary: A new indoor amusement concept called Play Town has been proposed for a site in Milford, Connecticut, adding to a pipeline of new FEC developments across the Northeast. The proposal signals continued investor and operator confidence in the indoor family entertainment format in suburban markets. FEC operators and real estate developers tracking new entrants in the Connecticut market should monitor this project's progress through local approval processes.

articles.title: Why Urban Design Principles May Better Explain Attraction Performance Than Experience Design
articles.summary: A thought-provoking analysis from Blooloop argues that urban design — how people move, orient themselves, and make choices within a space over time — may be a more powerful predictor of destination success than storytelling or architecture alone. For FEC operators and designers, the framework offers a fresh lens for evaluating guest flow, wayfinding, and spatial decision-making within their venues. The piece is particularly relevant for operators planning new builds or significant renovations.

articles.title: Blue Sky Thinking in Attraction Design: Starting With 'What If' Before 'How'
articles.summary: Creative directors from Forrec and Moment Factory discuss how blue sky thinking — allowing ideas to develop freely before applying operational or technical constraints — leads to more innovative and future-proof attraction designs. The session emphasizes that technology should serve storytelling and emotional connection rather than drive design decisions, a principle directly applicable to FEC attraction development. Operators and designers evaluating new attractions will find the framework useful for structuring early-stage concept development.

articles.title: Slick City Action Park Explained: A New Slide-Based Indoor Attraction Concept
articles.summary: A feature in the Fresno Bee breaks down what Slick City Action Park is — an indoor slide-based active entertainment concept that is expanding into new markets. The format, centered on a network of giant slides for all ages, represents a distinct niche within the active FEC category alongside trampoline parks and adventure courses. FEC operators evaluating new attraction categories should assess whether Slick City's format complements or competes with their existing offerings.
